blocks.text: LONDON, United Kingdom — “Human,” meaning to have the “qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines,” has been named the Cambridge Dictionary’s Word of the Year. In an era of rapidly expanding artificial intelligence (AI) and dire warnings that it could even wipe out humanity, the word captured “the 2026 zeitgeist,” Cambridge University Press board member Francesca Woodward told AFP. Over the past 12 months, people have been “really considering what it is to be human,” particularly because of concerns about AI taking over their jobs, she said. “I think people are trying to […]...
